statement.p: Find the slope of the tangent line to the curve \sqrt{x+3y}+\sqrt{6xy} = 9 at the point (3, 2).
The slope of the tangent line to the curve at the given point is .

solution.p: Differentiating implicitly with respect to x gives \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x+3y}} + \frac{3}{2 \sqrt{x+3y}} \, \frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{6}{2 \sqrt{6xy}} \left( y + x \, \frac{dy}{dx} \right) = 0, or (multiplying by 2 \sqrt{6xy} \sqrt{x+3y}) 1 \sqrt{6xy} + 3 \sqrt{6xy} \; \frac{dy}{dx} + 6 y \sqrt{x+3y} + 6 x \sqrt{x+3y} \; \frac{dy}{dx} = 0, so \left( 3 \sqrt{6xy} + 6 x \sqrt{x+3y} \right) \, \frac{dy}{dx} = - \left( 1 \sqrt{6xy} + 6 y \sqrt{x+3y} \right), and therefore \frac{dy}{dx} = - \frac {1 \sqrt{6xy} + 6 y \sqrt{x+3y}}{3 \sqrt{6xy} + 6 x \sqrt{x+3y}}. If x = 3 and y = 2, then \sqrt{x+3y} = 3, \sqrt{6xy} = 6, and hence the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point (3, 2) is \frac{dy}{dx} \Bigg|_{(x, y) = (3, 2)} = - \frac {1 \left( 6 \right) + 6 \left( 2 \right) \left( 3 \right)} {3 \left( 6 \right) + 6 \left( 3 \right) \left( 3 \right)} = -{\frac{7}{12}}.
